name: Limits_3
questiontext:
Evaluate the limit given below.

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}} {\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right) }.  \]

If the limit does not exist, enter the value 1111 as your answer.

The limit is: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
The limit of the function

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}} {\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right) }  \]

 is the same as the limit found by multiplying both numerator and denominator with the conjugate of the denominator:

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}} {\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}} \frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:4}}  \right) },  \]

which equals to

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}} {\left(\frac{{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} \right) },  \]

or, cancelling out the term in \( {{CT:6}} \), equals

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}} {\left( {{CT:7}} \right) } = {{CT:8}}.  \]
